findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Four cans of applesauce and two cans of black olives were observed with significant dents along the top or bottom seams. CORRECTED- PIC removed cans from storage to be returned to the suppliers for credit. Ensure cans are inspected for dents (along the top, bottom, and side seams) as they are stocked.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Kitchen is using a Envirox Concentrate 117 Sanitizer/Virucide Cleaner for some food contact surfaces. Cease use of this product for food contact since the label indicates it is for non-food contact surface use. CORRECTED- Facility will use quat sanitizer from the wall mounted dispenser over the 3 compartment sink for any food contact sanitizing purposes.
7-202.12: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be used according to manufacturer’s directions (indicate for use in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT). [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Quat sanitizer spray bottles observed with no measurable quat concentration. CORRECTED- Bottles refilled from the wall-mounted dispenser. Sanitizer observed at 200ppm quat. Use test strips to monitor and ensure sanitizer is an effective concentration.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 Dish machine chlorine rinse concentration was observed at 0ppm after the first ware washing cycle. It was determined the sanitizer was not dispensing during rinse cycle. Sanitizer lined was primed to remove air bubbles and allow for proper dispensing. After two additional ware washing cycles all chemicals were dispensing properly, and the chlorine rinse concentration was observed at 50-100ppm. Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris. Staff noted the can opener was last used during the previous day of operation. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. The manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed, including the use of a forearm to shut off the faucet to avoid re-contamination of hands after washing. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine final rinse concentration was observed at 10-25ppm. Chemicals were dispensing properly, and sanitizer was not diluted (concentrate bleached out test strip). Call for service was made during inspection. Dish machine will be used for wash and rinse prior to manually sanitizing at the 3 part sink with quat solution (200ppm) until the dish machine is serviced and once again able to properly sanitize dishes. Spot check will be conducted after the dish machine is serviced to verify proper function.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chlorine final rinse concentration at dish machine was observed at ~10ppm chlorine. After connecting fresh chemical and priming the machine, the concentration was observed just below 50ppm. Food Service Director will place a call for service to get the machine repaired. In the meantime, dishes will be washed and rinsed in the dish machine and manually sanitized at the 3 part sink using quat solution until the dish machine can maintain a proper final rinse concentration of 50-200ppm chlorine. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 Employee health paperwork is maintained in the manager's office at the elementary school. Signed reporting agreements were available for the high school staff but could not be located for the manager and elementary school staff. New reporting agreements were signed by the manager and elementary school staff during the inspection. Ensure signed reporting agreements are maintained on record for all food service staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine final rinse concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Sanitizer line was primed, and product was dispensing. Manager made a call for service and was advised the chemical in use may be old and need to be changed. Additional product was not available to change the sanitizer bucket during inspection. Manager ordered a gallon bucket of sanitizer from supplier. Dishes will be washed and rinsed in the dish machine and manually sanitized at the 3 part sink until the dish machine is observed to be providing proper final rinse concentration (50-200ppm).
A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions (no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm). Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

Spray bottle of quat sanitizer in the dish room was observed with a concentration below 100ppm. Solution was discarded. New solution was prepared and observed at 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration once foam settles out of freshly dispensed quat solution.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle of quat solution was 100ppm. Solution was prepared earlier in the week. Solution was discarded. New solution was prepared and observed at proper concentration of 200ppm. 
Check the solution in spray bottles with test strips to verify concentration is maintained during use. Change the solution in spray bottles as needed. 

Maintain quaternary ammonium compound solutions at a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of milk in the walkin cooler used to make ranch dressing was not date marked. Milk was opened the day prior and dated with a proper date mark of 1/24. 

Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be used or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41°F/less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date).

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.180 - Chicken breasts in warmer had surface and internal temperatures at 116°F and 122°F-124°F respectively. Chicken breasts were heated within the 30 minutes prior to inspector's arrival; the final cooking temperature was not checked prior to placing in the warmer for hot holding. Chicken breasts were placed back in the oven and heated to an internal temperature of 194°F prior to placing back in the warmer for hot holding.

All potentially hazardous foods shall be cooked to the proper product temperature. Chicken breasts are a pre-cooked product that are cooked from frozen. Make sure this product reaches an internal temperature of 135°F prior to hot holding.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Barrier was not used to shut off the manual faucet. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with staff; good handwashing technique was observed for the remainder of the inspection.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Sanitizer concentration was observed at 10ppm at the dish machine. Several full cycles were ran for the machine, and the chemical lines were primed. Inspector and Food Service Manager used two different sets of chlorine test strips and both verified a low concentration. Call for service was made, and a technician would be on-site after lunch to make repairs. In the meantime, the detergent was dispending properly. Dishes may be ran through the dish machine and manually sanitized at the 3 part sink if necessary until dish machine is properly dispensing sanitizer. Spot check will be conducted before the next routine inspection to check on status of dish machine repairs.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Spray bottle of sanitizer in prep area was observed at 0ppm quat. Solution was just used to wipe down a prep table. Solution was possibly prepared the week prior. Solution was emptied and new solution was obtained from the wall mounted chemical dispenser and observed at 400ppm. Prep table was wiped down with new sanitizer solution.

Maintain quat solution at 200-400ppm in spray bottles. Use test strips to verify concentration, and change the solution as needed (concentration will wear down over time).

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.160 - Staff were observed opening boxes with gloved hands prior to handling foods. One box contained fruit cups, which did not require glove use, but staff wear gloves due to the fact that some children open the fruit cups and drink the juice. The other box contained bagged fries that were portioned on trays and moved around with gloved hands. Staff were advised boxes are not considered clean surfaces. A better practice is to open all boxes prior to washing hands and putting on gloves for food handling.
Staff washed hands and put on new gloves to continue with food prep after boxes were removed from the area.

Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Can opener blade was observed to be soiled with buildup. Can opener was used the day prior and had not yet been through ware washing process. Can opener was placed through the dish machine during inspection.

To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) upright black fan by dish room (dust);   and
B) slicer - general surfaces beneath slicing attachments (food debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. Manually clean and sanitize all surfaces of the slicer that are unable to be placed through the dish machine for ware washing.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g -  Chlorine test kit was not available for checking sanitizer concentration at dish machine. Manager stated a new set of chlorine test strips would be purchased today.
Quat strips were available for checking wall mounted sanitizer (200ppm quat = bucket & bottles).

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Bulk food storage tubs are observed with dead bodies of bugs on the lids. Containers were empty. Items were immediately pulled for proper washing. See notes in General Comments. Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floor around the backdoor, beneath the chemical storage shelf in the dishroom, and especially the dry storage room are littered with bodies of dead bugs. Facility immediately began cleaning the floors during the inspection. Clean these flooring areas daily to insure pests are getting removed quickly. Monitor the dry storage room for entry points. Facility is new. Wall-to-floor gap should be check and possibly caulked to eliminate entry points. No entry points were noted during the inspection. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750-1300 Sanitizing bottle observed without label stored on the chemical storage shelf in the dishroom. Properly labeled with 'Sanitizer' during the inspection. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-820d 750-820d Observed the water level in the 3-compartment sink to be too low to totally submerged a large mixing bowl. Employee properly left bowl within sanitizer for the required time. The bowl was not removed from sanitizer by the employee. Water was added to the sink to allow required sanitizer concentration and water depth. Large bowls are usually placed through the dish machine.  Discussed testing and proper immersion with manager and employee.Observed sanitizer concentration in the third sink of the three compartment sink to be well over 200ppm Quat. During the inspection, water was added to the sink and the concentration of solution was tested at 200ppm Quat. Make sure that those test strips are used to monitoring sanitizer solution - especially when dealing with new process and equipment. Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: The sanitizer in the 3 part sink is reading 100ppm of quat. The temperature of the water is 62F. 750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).  Adjust the dispenser so that the water temperature is maintained at least 70F and the concentration in the sink is maintained at 200ppm of quat.  They are going to use the liquid quat from the other dispenser or use drop in tabs and abandon use of the dispenser above the sink until such time that it can be adjusted to function properly. Call for a spot check before use of the dispenser.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. One of the spoons in the clean utensil drawer has some soil. Check utensils after wash and before they are put away. If any soil remains return them to dish for proper cleaning.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. The back door to the kitchen is not tight fitting or self closing. Repair the door so that it is tight fitting and self closing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Two wet wiping cloths were observed to be sitting out. One on a prep table and the other on the clean dish drain area.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. It appears that a knife has been but away soiled.  Wash, rinse and sanitize all food contact equipment after each use or any time the equipment may have become contaminated.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. The bottom of the milk cooler has some water accumulating in it. Clean and keep clean.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. The drawer holding the afore mentioned soiled knife is soiled from the knife and must be washed, rinsed and sanitized so that it does not contaminate other clean utensils placed in the drawer.
